issues.failure_explanation: The implemented (normalized) indicator eta_j = ΔU_max/(ε+ΔU_max) saturates at ≈1 for any update larger than ε, so s_j = η_j^p/(η_j^p+τ^p) is effectively binary (≈1/(1+τ^p) whenever any update is present) and does not scale with the update magnitude. Hence the premise |s_j^n| ≤ C_s h^p of Proposition prop:local-consistency is never satisfied by the implemented method, and the local truncation error difference is only O(h), the same order as the base scheme — as the paper itself states in cor:normalized-accuracy and sec:blending-design. The higher-order conclusion of prop:local-consistency holds only for an unnormalized indicator that is discussed but never implemented. Nevertheless, the abstract, the introduction's 'Analytical results' paragraph, and the conclusion advertise the higher-order modification as an established property of the proposed mechanism.

failure_location.quote: When this parameter scales with the magnitude of the finite-volume update—as is the case for the shut-off mechanism we propose—the additional contribution of UM-SRD to the local truncation error is of higher order than that of the base first-order scheme.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to restrict the higher-order claim to the unnormalized indicator and to state that, for the implemented normalized indicator, the truncation-error difference is O(h) (same order as the base first-order scheme), leaving first-order accuracy as the supported accuracy statement. The paper's own body (cor:normalized-accuracy, sec:blending-design) already contains the correct content, so no new proof is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The headline analytical claim that UM-SRD's local truncation error modification is higher-order in smooth regions is withdrawn for the method the paper actually defines and implements; only the same-order O(h) bound and the numerically confirmed first-order convergence remain supported. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion misstate the scope of the theory relative to the paper's own corollary.
issues.title: Abstract/introduction/conclusion advertise a higher-order truncation-error modification that the implemented shut-off does not deliver
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained weakening of prose claims requiring no new proof architecture, and the supported first-order accuracy, conservation, shut-off, and (1D) TVD content all survive; the loss is limited to the higher-order smoothness selling point, which the paper's own corollary concedes does not apply to the implemented indicator.

issues.failure_explanation: The UM-SRD operator defined in the paper (Definition 'UM-SRD operator', the component form, and Algorithm alg:added-1) is U^{n+1} = R_j(s_j) U^* with U^* = B(U^n) the finite-volume update on the original cut-cell mesh, where the small cell has local CFL aΔt/(αh) = ν/α. Theorem thm:TVD-UMSRD instead proves TVD for the different composition pre-merge → finite-volume update on the merged mesh → blended redistribution (its proof steps 1–3), i.e., the Berger–Giuliani SRD time step. The operators genuinely differ: from U_{j-1}=1, U_j=0 (all other cells 0), ν=0.5, α=0.1, s_j=1, the defined algorithm gives U^{n+1}_{j-1}=U^{n+1}_j = (0.5+0.1·5)/1.1 ≈ 0.909, while the theorem's operator gives ≈ 0.496. For the defined operator the only available chain is TV(U^{n+1}) ≤ TV(U^*) ≤ TV(U^n); the second inequality is TVD of the original-mesh upwind scheme, which fails under the theorem's stated CFL aΔt/h ≤ 1 at the small cell, and the proof never analyzes the original-mesh update. The argument is valid but establishes TVD of a materially different time-stepping operator than the one stated, defined, and implemented.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either (a) prove TVD directly for the actual composed operator R_j(s_j)∘B on the original mesh under the full-mesh CFL aΔt/h ≤ 1 — a new analysis, since the base step is not TVD at the small cell under this CFL — or (b) restrict the theorem's CFL hypothesis to the cell-wise condition aΔt/Δx_i ≤ 1 for all i, forfeiting the advertised full-mesh-timestep stabilization regime that motivates the method.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central guarantee — TVD of UM-SRD under the base-scheme (full-mesh) CFL — is unproved for the algorithm the paper defines and tests (Experiment 5 uses the original-mesh base scheme that diverges under the full-mesh timestep). Consequently cor:normalized-accuracy loses the stability basis for its global first-order-accuracy conclusion; the algorithm's claimed TVD inheritance after alg:added-1, Experiment 3's TVD confirmation, and the abstract's TVD claim are all unreliable. Under the stronger cell-wise CFL aΔt/(αh) ≤ 1 the defined operator would be TVD from the existing propositions, but that excludes the advertised full-mesh-timestep stabilization regime.
issues.title: Theorem thm:TVD-UMSRD proves TVD for a merged-mesh finite-volume operator, not for the UM-SRD operator defined and implemented in the paper
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution either requires essentially new proof architecture (a direct TVD analysis of the composed original-mesh operator under the full-mesh CFL, whose success the source does not establish) or abandons the advertised regime (restricting to the small-cell CFL makes the base scheme itself TVD and the result vacuous relative to SRD's purpose). No local edit preserves the theorem's stated quantifier and regime.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's own weights (w_{i,j}=1, forced by the conservation constraint when W_i={j}), the neighborhood average is (hU_{j-1}+αhU_j)/(h+αh) = (U_{j-1}+αU_j)/(1+α), which is not equal to (1−α)U_{j-1}+αU_j for α∈(0,1) (e.g., α=0.2: coefficients 0.833/0.167 versus 0.8/0.2). The displayed identity is algebraically false. The same false simplification appears in the statement of Proposition prop:srd-steady, in the statement of Corollary cor:steady-accumulation, and in the proof of Proposition prop:local-consistency. Experiment 6 confirms the volume average: (1·1.5+0.2·2.5)/1.2 = 5/3 ≈ 1.667, not (1−0.2)·1.5+0.2·2.5 = 1.7.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (1−α)U_{j-1}+αU_j by (U_{j-1}+αU_j)/(1+α) in the two statements and in the proof of prop:local-consistency (equivalently [(S_j−I)V]_{j-1} = α(V_j−V_{j-1})/(1+α)); this is the unique correction consistent with the paper's weighted-average definition, its conservation constraint, and its own Experiment 6. No new argument is required and no conclusion changes.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed steady-state redistribution values in prop:srd-steady and the error-accumulation formulas in cor:steady-accumulation are numerically wrong (the correct coefficients are 1/(1+α) and α/(1+α)), and the proof of prop:local-consistency contains the same false step. All qualitative conclusions survive: SRD still fails to preserve steady states, errors are still replaced by their volume-weighted average, and (S_j−I)B(u^n) remains O(h), so the O(h^{p+1}) local-truncation-error conclusion of prop:local-consistency is unaffected.
issues.title: False algebraic identity for the neighborhood average: (U_{j-1} + αU_j)/(1+α) is equated to (1−α)U_{j-1} + αU_j
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local, forced correction — the source's own definitions and Experiment 6 pin down the unique right-hand side — and every substantive claim, rate, and guarantee survives unchanged; the issue is minor even though the false identity appears in formal statements.
